title: About the Handbook
text: This Handbook has been prepared to make employers aware of the new provisions in a simplified manner. It primarily covers provisions of the Codes for establishments under Central Government jurisdiction.
summary: This handbook is a simplified guide for Central Government establishments. It explains the four Labour Codes but is not a legal document—the Codes themselves prevail if there is any discrepancy.

title: Reforms Introduced under Labour Codes
text: Through the enactment of the four Labour Codes, 1,228 sections were streamlined into 480, and 1,436 rules reduced to 351. Multiple returns have been replaced with a single electronic return.
summary: Employers benefit from simpler compliance: fewer sections and rules, one unified electronic return, fewer forms and registers, and new measures like compounding of offences and improvement notices.

title: Code on Wages Overview
text: The Code on Wages, 2019 amalgamates four wage and payment related labour laws. It balances worker rights with ease of compliance for employers.
summary: This Code consolidates laws on minimum wages, equal pay, timely payment, overtime, bonus, and record-keeping.

title: Minimum Wages and Wage Payment
text: Employers must pay minimum wages notified by the government. When an employee leaves, all due wages must be paid within two working days.
summary: Practical effect: a worker can't be paid below the government-set floor, and if they quit, get fired, or are let go, the employer has a hard 2-day deadline to clear all outstanding dues — no waiting for the next payroll cycle.

title: Equal Remuneration and Non-Discrimination
text: Employers must not discriminate on the basis of gender in paying wages for the same or similar work, and must not discriminate on the basis of sex while recruiting employees.
summary: Workers have the right to equal pay for the same or similar work regardless of gender. Employers cannot discriminate by sex during recruitment or wage payment.

title: Wage Periods and Payment Timelines
text: Every establishment shall fix wage periods, which may be daily, weekly, fortnightly, or monthly. All wages must be paid within the prescribed timelines.
summary: Employers must choose a wage period and pay all wages within the deadlines set for that period.

title: Working Hours and Overtime
text: Employers must comply with daily and weekly working hour limits. If an employee works beyond normal hours, overtime must be paid at twice the normal wage.
summary: Workers who work beyond normal hours are entitled to overtime pay at double the normal wage rate.

title: Registers and Wage Slips
text: Employers must maintain attendance, wage, overtime, and deduction registers for five years, and issue wage slips to all employees on or before payment.
summary: Employers must keep accurate records of wages and attendance, and provide workers with wage slips showing pay details.

title: Notice Board and Deductions
text: Employers must display wage and inspection information in English, Hindi, and the local language. Deductions cannot exceed 50% of wages.
summary: Employers must display wage details and inspector information on notice boards in three languages. Only authorised deductions are allowed, capped at 50% of wages per period.

title: Bonus Provisions
text: Employees earning up to the prescribed wage limit and working at least 30 days in the year are entitled to an annual bonus between 8.33% and 20% of wages earned.
summary: Eligible workers must receive an annual bonus of at least 8.33% and up to 20% of their wages if they meet the wage ceiling and minimum work requirement.

title: Industrial Relations Code Overview
text: The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 consolidates provisions related to trade unions, employment conditions, and settlement of industrial disputes.
summary: This Code covers trade unions, grievance redressal, standing orders, lay-offs, retrenchment, closures, and strike or lockout procedures.

title: Works Committee
text: Employers of industrial establishments with 100 or more workers may be required to constitute a Works Committee to promote harmonious relations.
summary: Large industrial establishments (100+ workers) may need a Works Committee with equal or greater worker representation to maintain harmony.

title: Grievance Redressal Committee
text: Establishments with 20 or more workers must set up Grievance Redressal Committees to resolve employee grievances within 30 days.
summary: Workers can file grievances within one year, and the committee must resolve them within 30 days.

title: Standing Orders
text: Industrial establishments with 300 or more workers must adopt Model Standing Orders or certify their own within six months.
summary: Large establishments (300+ workers) must have certified Standing Orders governing service conditions.

title: Recognition of Negotiating Union or Council
text: If multiple unions exist, the one with 51% support is recognised. Otherwise, a Negotiating Council is formed.
summary: Workers' collective bargaining is handled through a majority union or a Negotiating Council if no union holds majority support.

title: Notice for Change of Service Conditions
text: Employers must give 21 days' notice before changing wages, hours, leave, discipline rules, or workforce size.
summary: Workers must receive 21 days' written notice before employers change listed service conditions.

title: Lay-off, Retrenchment and Closure — 50 to 299 Workers
text: Industrial establishments employing 50 to 299 workers must notify the government before lay-off, retrenchment, or closure. Retrenchment compensation is 15 days' average pay per year of service.
summary: Mid-size establishments must notify government before lay-off, retrenchment, or closure. Workers get 50% wages during lay-off and 15 days' pay per year of service if retrenched.

title: Lay-off, Retrenchment and Closure — 300 or More Workers
text: Industrial establishments with 300+ workers must obtain prior government permission before lay-off, retrenchment, or closure. Employers must give three months' notice before retrenchment.
summary: Large establishments need prior government approval for lay-off, retrenchment, or closure. Workers receive three months' notice and compensation plus reskilling fund support.

title: Mandatory Notice of Strike or Lockout
text: Employers must report strike or lockout notices to government authorities and the Conciliation Officer within five days.
summary: Employers must report strike and lockout notices within five days, or immediately if action is already underway.

title: OSH and Working Conditions Code Overview
text: The OSH&WC Code, 2020 consolidates 13 Central Labour laws into one comprehensive legislation. It ensures safe and healthy working conditions in establishments with 10 or more workers.
summary: This Code unifies 13 safety and working-conditions laws with single registration, all-India licensing, and electronic filings for establishments with 10+ workers.

title: Establishment Registration
text: Every establishment employing 10 or more employees must apply for registration within 60 days of its existence. The application will be made electronically on the portal prescribed by the appropriate Government.
summary: Employers with 10+ employees must register electronically within 60 days of starting operations and update registration details within 30 days of any change.

title: Notice of Commencement and Cessation of Operation
text: Employers must send an electronic notice of commencement or cessation of operations of establishments such as factories, mines, contract labour establishments, or construction sites.
summary: Employers must electronically notify authorities when factories, mines, contract labour establishments, or construction sites begin or cease operations.

title: Core Duties of Employer
text: Every employer shall issue appointment letters to all employees, provide annual health check-ups free of cost, and ensure the workplace is free from hazards likely to cause injury or disease.
summary: Employers must give appointment letters, provide free annual health check-ups, and keep workplaces safe from hazards.

title: Safety Committees and Safety Officers
text: Every establishment must constitute a Safety Committee with representatives of both employer and workers. Large construction sites (250+ workers) and mines (100+ workers) must appoint safety officers.
summary: Employers must form Safety Committees and appoint safety officers in large construction sites and mines.

title: Safety, Health and Welfare Facilities
text: Employers must maintain safe and healthy workplaces with cleanliness, ventilation, lighting, safe drinking water, and separate toilets. Establishments with 50+ workers must provide a crèche; those with 100+ must provide a canteen.
summary: Workers are entitled to safe, hygienic workplaces with welfare facilities. Larger establishments must provide crèches and canteens.

title: OSH Registers, Records and Returns
text: Employers must maintain registers of employees, attendance, wages, overtime, deductions, and dangerous occurrences. They must file annual returns electronically.
summary: Employers must keep prescribed registers and file annual electronic returns with the government.

title: Reporting Accidents, Dangerous Occurrences and Diseases
text: Employers must notify authorities of any workplace accident causing death, serious injury, or prescribed incidents. They must also report scheduled occupational diseases.
summary: Employers must promptly report workplace deaths, serious injuries, dangerous occurrences, and occupational diseases.

title: Women Working at Night and in Dangerous Operations
text: Women may work in all establishments and roles. For night shifts, employers must obtain consent and ensure safety measures. Pregnant women may be restricted from hazardous work.
summary: Women can work night shifts with consent and safety safeguards. Pregnant women may be restricted from hazardous operations.

title: Common Licence for Factories, Contract Labour and Beedi Work
text: Employers may apply electronically for a common licence covering factories, contract labour, and beedi/cigar work instead of separate licences.
summary: Employers and contractors can obtain a unified electronic licence covering multiple types of work.

title: Contract Labour Provisions
text: Establishments with 50+ contract workers must comply with licensing rules. If contractors fail to pay wages, the principal employer is liable to pay.
summary: When 50+ contract workers are used, contractors must be licensed and principal employers must ensure wages and welfare facilities.

title: Inter-State Migrant Workers
text: These provisions apply to establishments employing 10 or more inter-state migrant workers. Employers must pay each worker an annual lump-sum journey allowance.
summary: Employers with 10+ inter-state migrant workers must provide an annual travel allowance between the workplace and the worker's native place.

title: Additional Provisions for Mines
text: Employers must ensure safe workplaces and appoint a Welfare Officer in mines employing 250+ workers. Medical examinations must be conducted as prescribed.
summary: Mine operators must maintain safe workplaces, appoint welfare officers in large mines, and conduct medical checks for workers.

title: Additional Provisions for Major Docks
text: Employers must comply with occupational safety and health standards and regulations notified by the Central Government for major docks.
summary: Dock employers must follow Central Government safety and health standards specific to dock operations.

title: Additional Provisions for Building and Construction Workers
text: Employers must provide free temporary accommodation at or near worksites. Workers with impairments posing accident risks must not be employed in hazardous construction tasks.
summary: Construction employers must provide free site accommodation and restrict hazardous work for workers with impairments that increase accident risk.

title: Social Security Code Overview
text: The Code on Social Security, 2020 subsumes nine labour laws, covering EPFO, ESIC, gratuity, maternity benefit, compensation, welfare cess, and social security for unorganised, gig, and platform workers.
summary: This Code consolidates provident fund, insurance, gratuity, maternity, compensation, and welfare schemes into one framework.

title: Employees' Provident Fund
text: Applies to establishments with 20+ employees. Employers must contribute 10% of wages to the Provident Fund scheme.
summary: Establishments with 20+ employees must register for EPF. Both employer and employee contribute 10% of wages toward provident fund, pension, and insurance.

title: Employees' State Insurance
text: Applies to establishments with 10+ employees, except seasonal factories. Employers must pay both employer and employee contributions.
summary: Eligible establishments must provide ESI coverage. Employers pay contributions, giving workers sickness, maternity, disablement, medical, and funeral benefits.

title: Gratuity
text: Employees completing five years of continuous service (one year for fixed-term contracts) are entitled to gratuity at 15 days' wages per year of service.
summary: Workers with five years of service (one year for fixed-term) must receive gratuity at 15 days' wages per year, payable within 30 days.

title: Maternity Benefit
text: Women employees with at least 80 days of service in the preceding year are entitled to 26 weeks of maternity benefit.
summary: Practical effect: a pregnant worker with enough service history doesn't lose her job or income for taking leave — she gets ~6 months paid time off, can't be dismissed for being pregnant, gets short breaks to nurse after returning, and larger employers must provide crèche access.

title: Employees' Compensation
text: Employers must pay compensation for work-related injury or death, including commuting accidents. Compensation must be deposited with the competent authority.
summary: Workers injured or killed in work-related accidents, including commuting, are entitled to compensation deposited with authorities.

title: Social Security for Gig and Platform Workers
text: The Social Security Code introduces the concept of gig and platform workers. Aggregators must contribute between 1% and 2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of total payments to workers.
summary: Gig and platform workers are legally recognised. Aggregator platforms must contribute part of turnover toward their social security.

title: Building and Other Construction Workers — Welfare Cess
text: Employers must pay a cess of 1–2% of construction cost to fund social security and welfare benefits. Workers must be registered with the Welfare Board.
summary: Construction employers must pay a welfare cess and register workers with the Welfare Board.

title: Employment Exchanges and Career Centres
text: Governments may require employers to report vacancies to career centres before filling them. Reporting does not oblige recruitment through the centre.
summary: Employers may need to notify job vacancies to government career centres, but hiring through them is optional.

title: Foundational Compliance Actions
text: Employers must register establishments, display mandatory notices, maintain registers, fix wage periods, ensure safety measures, start EPF/ESIC registration, and constitute committees.
summary: On day one, employers must complete registration, display notices, set up registers and committees, ensure safety basics, and initiate social security registrations.

title: Monthly Compliance Actions
text: Employers must pay wages on time, deposit EPF/ESIC contributions, issue wage slips, and update registers monthly.
summary: Each month employers must pay wages, remit EPF/ESI contributions, issue wage slips, and keep registers updated.

title: Annual and Periodical Compliance Actions
text: Employers must file unified annual returns, update minimum wage rates, renew licences, conduct safety audits, and provide annual health examinations.
summary: Each year employers must file returns, refresh wage compliance, renew licences, and conduct safety audits and health check-ups.

title: Event-Based Compliance Actions
text: Employers must report accidents and diseases promptly, issue appointment letters, settle final dues, and seek government permission for lay-offs or closures in large establishments.
summary: During events like accidents, hiring, exits, or closures, employers must take immediate prescribed actions including reporting and settlement of dues.

title: Key Definitions — Wages and Employee
text: Wages include basic pay, dearness allowance, and retaining allowance, with exclusions capped at 50%. Employee means any person employed on wages to perform work.
summary: Wages include basic pay and allowances, with exclusions limited to half of pay. Most hired workers qualify as employees under the Wages Code.

title: Key Definitions — Worker under IR Code
text: Worker means any person employed in industry to do manual, skilled, technical, operational, clerical or supervisory work, excluding managers and supervisors earning above Rs. 18,000 per month.
summary: Most industrial employees are covered as workers under the IR Code, except senior managers and high-paid supervisors.

title: Third Schedule — Conditions Requiring 21-Day Notice
text: The Third Schedule lists the specific conditions of service that trigger the 21-day notice rule: wages, working hours, leave, discipline procedures, and changes to workforce size or shift arrangements.
summary: This is the reference schedule behind the 21-day notice requirement in Section 16 — it spells out exactly which changes require advance notice.

title: Third Schedule — Notifiable Occupational Diseases
text: Employers must notify authorities when workers contract listed occupational diseases such as silicosis, asbestosis, or occupational cancer.
summary: Employers must report scheduled occupational diseases to authorities within the prescribed timeframe.

title: First Schedule — Social Security Applicability
text: EPF applies to establishments with 20+ employees. ESI applies to establishments with 10+ employees (excluding seasonal factories). Gratuity applies to factories, mines, plantations, ports, railways, and shops with 10+ employees.
summary: The First Schedule sets thresholds: EPF at 20+ employees, ESI at 10+, and gratuity/maternity at factories and shops with 10+ employees.
